member.name: T:OpenIGI.Platform.IFramePacer
member.summary: Holds a loop to a frame rate, where the platform leaves that to the loop.
member.remarks: A desktop loop renders as fast as it is let, and a screen that changes no faster than the display shows it -- the menu -- is held to the display's rate by waiting out each frame's remainder. A browser paces every frame itself, from its animation callback, and a loop that also waited would halve its own rate at best and hang the page at worst; there the pacer does nothing.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Platform.IFramePacer.Pace(System.Int32)
member.summary: Waits until the current frame's interval has elapsed, then schedules the next.
member.param: The rate to hold to; nothing happens at or below zero.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Platform.IFramePacer.Reset
member.summary: Forgets the cadence, so the next starts fresh rather than catching up.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Platform.IGameWindow
member.summary: The host window: a surface to render into, a message pump, and the input state that pump feeds.

remarks.para: The original's window lives in WinMain (0x48F530) and its message loop drives everything: it pumps messages, then calls the root task's update, then repeats. This interface keeps that shape — is the message pump, and the caller owns the loop, so the game loop's frame arbiter stays in charge of when work happens.
All members must be called from the thread that created the window.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Platform.IGameWindow.CursorLocked
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the cursor is held inside the window.
member.remarks: A locked cursor is hidden and cannot leave, so mouse motion keeps arriving however far the user drags. That is what a look-around control needs: without it the pointer reaches the edge of the screen and the view stops turning. Merely hiding the cursor is not enough, which is why this is separate from .

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Platform.IGameWindow.ClipboardText
member.summary: Gets or sets the system clipboard's text.

remarks.para: On the window because the clipboard belongs to the windowing system, not to the input devices: the platform backend already owns the handle that reaches it, and putting it here keeps every layer above free of a platform reference. A host that cannot reach a clipboard returns an empty string and discards what is set, so a caller never has to ask whether one exists.
Reading is a synchronous call into the window system and is not free; read it when a paste is actually asked for rather than polling it.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Platform.IGameWindow.IsFocused
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the window has input focus.
member.remarks: The original releases every key when its input device cannot be read, which is what focus loss looks like from the inside; hosts should clear the same way rather than leaving keys latched down.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Platform.WindowMode
member.summary: How a game window relates to the screen it is on.
member.remarks: The original only knows two of these: WinMain creates a WS_POPUP window covering the screen unless -window was passed, and the Direct3D device is then created in exclusive mode. is an addition — the same screen-covering picture without taking the display away from the desktop compositor, which is what alt-tabbing out of a modern build is expected to feel like.

member.remarks: The display mode is not changed, so the picture is composited at whatever resolution and refresh rate the desktop is running at. Switching away is instant and nothing else on the machine is resized, which is the point of it.
